extracted.intended_audience: Developers/contributors writing Python/Cython code and documentation for the SageMath project
extracted.subtask_description: Contributing code and documentation to the Sage library: Python/Cython source files, docstrings, tests, packaging, and repository practices conforming to Sage project conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow standard Python formatting rules (PEP 8 / PEP 257)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the standard Python formatting rules when writing code for Sage, as explained at the following URLs: PEP 0008, PEP 0257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 4 spaces for indentation levels. Do not use tabs. Many editors can insert 4 spaces for Tab. Adhere to PEP8 line-length and docstring conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation: use 4 spaces, not tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 4 spaces for indentation levels. Do not use tabs as they can result in indentation confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most editors can be configured to insert 4 spaces when Tab is hit. Also many editors will automatically search/replace leading tabs with 4 spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace conventions in expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitespace before and after assignment and binary operator of the lowest priority in the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: i = i + 1 ; c = (a+b) * (a-b). No whitespace before or after the = sign if it is used for keyword arguments: def complex(real, imag=0.0): return magic(r=real, i=imag). No whitespace immediately inside parenthesis, brackets, and braces: spam(ham[1], {eggs: 2}) ; [i^2 for i in range(3)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Function and class naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use all lowercase function names with words separated by underscores; use CamelCase for class names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example function naming: def set_some_value():. Exception: some functions have uppercase letters where it makes sense (e.g., Matrix_integer_dense.LLL). Factory functions that mimic object constructors (e.g., PolynomialRing) may be CamelCase.

rubrics_metrics.name: File and directory naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Python Sage library code goes into src/sage/ and uses conventions: directory names may be plural and file names are almost always singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If creating a new package directory, include __init__.py and an all.py listing user-facing imports. Prefer creating subpackages rather than adding new top-level packages. Example: file polynomial_ring.py may contain several types of polynomial rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package data and non-Python files guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Python Sage source code and small supporting files can be included in the directory of the Python code or in src/sage/ext_data/; there are preferred ways to access these resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred access: importlib.resources.files().joinpath(...).open('rt'/'rb'), read_text(), read_bytes(), or importlib.resources.as_file() for files used outside Python. Use ext_data only where appropriate; practice of ext_data is deprecated. Files must be listed in options.package_data of setup metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large data files must be externalized (do not add large files to source tree)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large data files should not be added to the Sage source tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended procedure: create a separate git repository, make it pip-installable, upload to PyPI, and add metadata in SAGE_ROOT/build/pkgs to make the package known to Sage. See Packaging Third-Party Code for Sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All code included with Sage must be licensed under the GPLv2+ or a compatible (less restrictive) license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of compatible licenses include the BSD license. Include proper license header in files as demonstrated in the template header block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-of-file header and AUTHORS section format
rubrics_metrics.description: The top of each Sage code file should include a short one-line summary, paragraph description, EXAMPLES, and an AUTHORS list with entries like 'Your Name (YYYY-MM-DD): description'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a raw string docstring r"""...""" at the top. Provide AUTHORS with concise entries; avoid verbosity. The authoritative history is in git/blame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring required elements: one-sentence description
rubrics_metrics.description: Every function must have a docstring that includes a one-sentence description of the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-sentence description must be followed by a blank line and end in a period. Describe the function's effect as a command (imperative), e.g., 'Return whether this integer is prime.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring: INPUT and OUTPUT blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings must include an INPUT and an OUTPUT block describing the input/output of the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INPUT: list arguments with descriptive type names (use 'integer' rather than 'int' if behavior-like). Mention default values when applicable. OUTPUT: required if the one-sentence description needs more explanation; describe multiple return items clearly (e.g., 'a tuple of - ... - ...'). Be verbose enough for complicated outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring: EXAMPLES block is required
rubrics_metrics.description: An EXAMPLES block for examples is not optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples are used both for documentation and are tested before each release (like TESTS). Provide many illustrative examples, show exceptions where appropriate, and ensure examples have good coverage of functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring: TESTS block recommended and format
rubrics_metrics.description: A TESTS block is highly recommended and contains tests not relevant to users (private test cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TESTS blocks are formatted like EXAMPLES and may be stripped for certain help contexts. Include corner cases and input validation tests. To use pytest in doctests, add 'TESTS: pytest' to the docstring so the method is explicitly marked as tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring: SEEALSO, ALGORITHM, NOTE, WARNING, TODO, PLOT, REFERENCES blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings may include specialized blocks: SEEALSO (highly recommended), ALGORITHM (optional), NOTE/WARNING/TODO/PLOT/REFERENCES (optional) to structure documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALGORITHM should indicate what algorithm/software is used and may include bibliographic references to be added to the master bibliography. NOTE/WARNING/TODO/PLOT have specific formats; e.g., .. NOTE:: must be uppercase and formatted correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx/reST directives: uppercase and exact form
rubrics_metrics.description: All reST and Sphinx directives (like .. WARNING::, .. NOTE::, .. MATH::, etc.) are written in uppercase and with the exact syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, WARNING:: or '.. WARNING ::' will not work. The main Sphinx directives used in Sage must be written exactly as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstrings: use raw strings and LaTeX typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: You are strongly encouraged to use LaTeX typesetting and raw strings (r"""...""") for docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For LaTeX commands containing backslashes, prefer raw strings so backslashes need not be doubled. Use MATH blocks for larger math; use :nowrap: when embedding align environments that should not be wrapped in gather. Balance readability for interactive console users (LaTeX code may be less readable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code fragments quoted with double backticks in docs
rubrics_metrics.description: Code fragments are quoted with double backticks in documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes function arguments and Python literals like ``True``, ``False``, and ``None``. For example: If ``check`` is ``True``, then ...

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples as tested doctests: write testable examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests have a double purpose: illustrate usage and serve as tests that are checked before each release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All new doctests must pass (e.g., running sage -t your_file.py should not give errors). Tests should include interesting examples, corner cases (0, one-element groups), and input validation checks. Examples must be verbose and demonstrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private functions naming and docstring policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions with names starting with an underscore are considered private and do not appear in the reference manual; their docstring should not contain information crucial for Sage users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can make private docstrings be part of another method's documentation (use .. automethod::). Private functions should still contain an EXAMPLES (or TESTS) block. Special case: __init__ docstring can serve as class docstring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master bibliography usage and citation key format
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographical references should be stored in the master bibliography file SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/references/index.rst with a citation key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation key format: for one author, first three letters of family name + year; for multiple authors, first letter of each family name + year. Use full four-digit year. When abbreviating first names, put a backslash in front (e.g., \C. F. Gauss). Use trailing underscore in docstrings to create hyperlinks to references (e.g., [Gau1801]_).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage documentation style constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage documentation is written in reStructuredText and processed by Sphinx; follow specific style rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines should be shorter than 80 characters. All Sphinx directives must be uppercase. Code fragments use double backticks. Be mindful of readability in interactive help vs HTML/PDF outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lazy_import for top-level all.py when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing user-facing imports in a package's all.py, prefer the lazy_import framework rather than direct imports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: from sage.misc.lazy_import import lazy_import; lazy_import(('sage.measure_theory.borel_measure', 'BorelMeasure'), ...). This avoids eagerly importing heavy modules at startup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage developer etiquette for style disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where fine stylistic points differ (e.g., one vs two spaces after sentences, tight vs spaced lists), acknowledge differences and respect the style of the author who first wrote the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to force a global preference; respect historical choices unless there is a compelling reason to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx MATH block handling and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: MATH blocks are translated to LaTeX environments; be aware of wrapping and readability concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using LaTeX environments like align that would be wrapped in gather, add a :nowrap: flag to the MATH mode. Keep LaTeX readable for interactive users where possible (prefer math expressions like a/b or a b^{-1} if \frac{}{} is less readable in help).

rubrics_metrics.name: TESTS block delimiting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a TESTS block: starts with 'TESTS:' and ends with a line indented less than 'TESTS' or by special markers such as Sphinx directives or uppercase headers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'TESTS' block ends either with a line indented less than 'TESTS', or with a line with the same level of indentation matching a Sphinx directive (.. foo:), an UPPERCASE: line, or a reST header marker line (e.g., a line of hyphens). Lines containing only double colons :: do not end TESTS blocks.
